# Fabrication notes: p

Generated by aethelgard 0.1.0 from the specification whose sha256 is
`SPEC_SHA`.
`MANIFEST.json` names every other file of this package by sha256, and the
verdict of the `aethelgard verify` run that emitted the package names every
file, `MANIFEST.json` included. `aethelgard verify --spec <file> --scenarios
<the files MANIFEST.json names> --against-fab <this directory>`, with the
other arguments of the run that emitted it, derives the package again and
names every file that differs. `MANIFEST.json` also names that run's verdict
by sha256, and the verdict states the sandbox each tool ran in, so a run
under another uid or user namespace finds `MANIFEST.json` different while
every other file is the same.

## What this package is

It was emitted by a passing `aethelgard verify`: every gate that verdict
names passed on the design generated from the specification, and these
files were made from that design. The gates judged the design, not these
files. It claims nothing beyond that verdict. Emitting this package made
no board, and nothing in it was tested on hardware.

The Gerbers are KiCad 10.0.7's output (`kicad-cli pcb export gerbers
--check-zones`), exported from a copy of the generated board with the
sha256 the design-rule gate judged, prepared as that gate prepares its copy
(the specification's rules), with every zone refilled by KiCad. KiCad writes the time of export into two lines of every Gerber
(`%TF.CreationDate` and `G04 Created by KiCad ... date`). Those two lines
are removed so that the package is reproducible; nothing else in any file
is changed. The drill file (`kicad-cli pcb export drill
--excellon-min-header`) and the placement file (`kicad-cli pcb export pos
--format csv --units mm --side both`) are KiCad's output, unchanged. KiCad's
Gerber job file is not included; this file states the stackup.

## Stackup

- 4 copper layers, top to bottom, joined only by through vias:
  - F.Cu: signal
  - In1.Cu: plane, net GND
  - In2.Cu: plane, net VDD_3V3
  - B.Cu: signal
- Each dielectric at least:
  - F.Cu to In1.Cu: 0.179 mm (OSH Park 4-layer, docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/, read 14 Nov 2026: 2113 prepreg 0.1999 mm less 0.0202 mm, rounded down)
  - In1.Cu to In2.Cu: 0.891 mm (OSH Park 4-layer, docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/, read 14 Nov 2026: FR408HR core 0.9906 mm less 0.0991 mm, rounded down)
  - In2.Cu to B.Cu: 0.179 mm (OSH Park 4-layer, docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/, read 14 Nov 2026: 2113 prepreg 0.1999 mm less 0.0202 mm, rounded down)
- Thickness source: OSH Park 4-layer, docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/, read 14 Nov 2026: min the dielectric minima summed; max dielectrics and resist at max plus 4 x 70 um copper, 1.8505 mm up. Copper source: the engine's stated condition (AET-WO-1305, as the reference): 2 oz, twice KiCad's 35 um; OSH Park publishes no copper tolerance.
- Every minimum here is its source's value less its published tolerance, rounded down; every maximum, rounded up.
- Laminate: as the dielectrics' sources above state, with laminate and solder mask relative permittivity at
  most 5.4 (the IPC-4101 FR-4 maximum, specified at 1 MHz).
- Declared thickness 1.6 mm. Finished board from 1.25 mm to 1.851 mm thick.
- Finished copper at most 70 um thick on each layer.

A board made outside this stackup is not covered by the capacitance bound
of `aethelgard extract`. That bound's scope and conditions, as `extract`
states them:

- scope: the bare board's copper and each I2C pin's Ci; part bodies, solder and terminations above the pads are not included
- laminate and solder mask relative permittivity at most 5.4 (the IPC-4101 FR-4 maximum, specified at 1 MHz)
- finished copper at most 70 um thick; finished board from 1.25 mm to 1.851 mm thick
- each dielectric at least its declared minimum: F.Cu to In1.Cu 0.179 mm, In1.Cu to In2.Cu 0.891 mm, In2.Cu to B.Cu 0.179 mm
- zone fill keeps the board's clearance (the DRC gate refills and judges it)
- every I2C pin at most UM10204's Ci of 10 pF; no multiplexer or switch on the line
- neighbouring nets are static while the line rises


## Holes

Every hole is a plated via, drilled 0.3 mm, with a 0.6 mm pad, but where a net class below declares its own via. The
drill file is Excellon, metric, with decimal coordinates, and its minimal
header carries no plating comment.

## Rule minima

- Track width: 0.2 mm.
- Copper to copper: 0.2 mm.
- Via: 0.6 mm pad, 0.3 mm drill.
- Net class `power` (VDD_3V3, GND): track width 0.25 mm, via 0.7 mm pad, 0.3 mm drill.

## Files

- `p-B_Cu.gbl`: Gerber, bottom copper
- `p-B_Mask.gbs`: Gerber, bottom solder mask
- `p-B_Paste.gbp`: Gerber, bottom solder paste
- `p-B_Silkscreen.gbo`: Gerber, bottom silkscreen
- `p-Edge_Cuts.gm1`: Gerber, board outline
- `p-F_Cu.gtl`: Gerber, top copper
- `p-F_Mask.gts`: Gerber, top solder mask
- `p-F_Paste.gtp`: Gerber, top solder paste
- `p-F_Silkscreen.gto`: Gerber, top silkscreen
- `p-In1_Cu.g1`: Gerber, inner copper layer 1, a plane (see Stackup)
- `p-In2_Cu.g2`: Gerber, inner copper layer 2, a plane (see Stackup)
- `p-pos.csv`: placement: reference, value, package, X and Y in mm, rotation, side
- `p.bom.csv`: bill of materials, as `aethelgard emit` writes it
- `p.drl`: Excellon drill file
- `p.elf`: firmware: the ELF `build` produced, whose sha256 is the verdict's `elf_sha256`
